reuse.why: All four steps extend the existing applyWeekendRule and recurConfigToRSchedule/RSchedule machinery, and the new range handler reuses them; only the template adds a small wrapper that re-checks skipWeekend which applyWeekendRule already checks.

duplication.why: Weekend, daily-skip and holiday logic is defined once in applyWeekendRule; getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange repeat a small occurrences-flatMap-applyWeekendRule block.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts, the new handler in server/schedules/app.ts beside getUpcomingDates, and the holidays field on RecurConfig and the RSchedule data, following the tree's layers.

scope.why: Edits stay on weekend handling, the new handler, the config type and tests.

maintainability.why: A single nullable applyWeekendRule is easy to follow, but callers carry hard-coded look-ahead windows (7, count*7, plus or minus 2 days) whose assumptions the later holiday step silently invalidates, and getNextDate rebuilds the rule object from differently named data fields.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every site resolves dates through applyWeekendRule; getWeekendAdjustedDay in schedule-template.ts is a thin wrapper over it.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated flatMap(applyWeekendRule) in getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange is short and visible, not reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: applyWeekendRule's rule object gained frequency and holidays and one daily branch returning null; these carry the requested rule itself, and all call sites (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, schedule-template) go through it.
